names.official: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe

summary: São Tomé and Príncipe exempts citizens of the EU, the US, Canada and the Portuguese-speaking CPLP countries from visas under Law 5/2015, and the UK, US and Canadian governments give their citizens 15 days visa-free; other nationalities apply online for an eVisa before arrival.

AO.notes: Visa-free: Law 5/2015 (article 25(1)(e) of the Foreigners Act) exempts citizens of the EU, the United States, Canada and the CPLP member states from visas. The law sets no length of stay; the UK, US and Canadian governments give 15 days for their own citizens. For a longer stay, apply for the eVisa before travelling or ask the Migration and Border Service for an extension.

tips.text: The UK, US and Canadian governments give their citizens a visa-free stay of 15 days, and the exemption law sets no other length. For a longer stay, apply for the eVisa before travelling or ask the Migration and Border Service for an extension soon after arrival.

Bring enough cash: the UK FCDO says cards are not widely accepted and ATMs are few, and Canada says foreign bank cards cannot be used to withdraw money from ATMs. Banks exchange US dollars, euros and CFA francs.

Canada's travel advice says malaria is a risk in São Tomé and Príncipe and that antimalarial medication is recommended for most travellers — see a health professional before you go and use insect repellent.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: Citizens of the EU, the US, Canada and the Portuguese-speaking CPLP countries are exempt from visas under Law 5/2015. The UK government says British visitors need no visa for up to 15 days, and the US and Canadian governments give their citizens the same 15 days; the law itself sets no length of stay. No official source we could read covers Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Switzerland. Everyone else — and anyone staying longer — applies online for an eVisa on the Migration and Border Service (SMF) e-visa portal before arrival.

faq.question: How can I stay longer than 15 days?
faq.answer: Apply for the eVisa before travelling (typically allowing stays of up to 30 days), or ask the Migration and Border Service in São Tomé for an extension before your permitted stay ends: under Law 5/2008 (article 43), visitors admitted without a visa can be given up to 30 days more, renewable once for the same period.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination required for São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — which covers most nearby mainland departure points such as Gabon, Angola or Ghana. Arriving directly from Europe, no certificate is needed, but carry the yellow card if your routing touches the mainland.

faq.question: What money should I bring to São Tomé and Príncipe?
faq.answer: Bring cash. The UK FCDO says credit cards are not widely accepted and ATMs are few; Canada says foreign bank cards cannot be used at ATMs and that banks exchange US dollars, euros and Central African CFA francs.
